title: Cohomological support
statement:
For a complex $K$ of sheaves on the small pro-etale site
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] with cohomology sheaves
[def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] $\mathcal H^r(K)$, the *cohomological
support* is the set of degrees in which the cohomology does not vanish:

$$
 \operatorname{Supp}_{\mathrm{coh}}(K)
 =\{r\in\mathbf Z:\mathcal H^r(K)\neq0\}.
$$

split_report.summary: Checked against the blueprint (master; slopmaster2 has no Lean and no separate text for it). The statement is kept: for K in D(Y_proet,A) it is the set of r with H^r(K) nonzero. It is built from D(Y_proet,A) [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], the cohomology sheaves H^r [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves], and the general notion for an object of the derived category of an abelian category, written as the new Mathlib leaf def-weil-derived-category-cohomological-support (also records amplitude in [a,b], the form in which the users def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed and thm-trf-trace-formula-e use it). Mathlib has no named support set; the item is the one-line specialization {r | ¬ IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor C r).obj K)} with C = Sh(Y_proet,A), and containment in [a,b] is DerivedCategory.IsGE a ∧ IsLE b via isGE_iff/isLE_iff. CochainComplex.IsStrictlyLE/GE (vanishing of the terms) is a different notion and is not used. The statement mentions 'complex of sheaves' while the H^r node is stated on D(Y_proet,A); since H^r is invariant under quasi-isomorphism these agree.
